title: Lab: copy a big model's thinking into a small one
summary: Fine-tune Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on about a thousand R1-style reasoning traces from an open dataset, using TRL's SFTTrainer and LoRA on a free Colab T4, then compare accuracy, format and answer length before and after on unseen GSM8K problems.
learningObjectives: Choose an openly licensed dataset of reasoning traces and inspect it before training.
Rewrite teacher traces into a <think>/<answer> conversational prompt-completion dataset for TRL.
Filter traces by token length to fit a free T4, and explain how filtering shapes the student's style.
Configure SFTTrainer with LoRA, completion-only loss and fp16 for a T4.
Measure accuracy, format rate and answer length before and after training with greedy decoding on held-out problems.
Read student replies to tell copied style apart from copied skill.

studyGuide.mentalModel: You're giving a student a stack of a top student's marked exam scripts and asking them to practise writing answers exactly like those scripts, word by word. You picked the stack, so you decide what they copy: if you only hand over the neat, shorter scripts, that's the style they'll learn. Then you give them a fresh exam they've never seen, and compare the marks, the neatness and how much they write, with their marks from before.
keyIdeas: Sequence-level distillation is just SFT on a teacher's saved traces; the teacher model doesn't need to run.
We used camel-ai/gsm8k_distilled (MIT): about 7,500 GSM8K training problems with R1-style <think> traces and a boxed answer.
Each trace is rewritten as a prompt (system + problem) and a completion (<think>…</think><answer>N</answer>) in chat-message form.
Traces longer than 1,024 tokens are dropped to fit a T4; this also biases the student toward the teacher's shorter answers.
LoRA trains small add-on matrices, completion_only_loss grades only the reply, and fp16 replaces bf16 on a T4.
Evaluation uses greedy decoding on the GSM8K test split, which the traces never saw, and records accuracy, format and tokens.
Format and length often change before accuracy does; accuracy is the honest measure of copied skill.
misconceptions: "Distillation needs access to the teacher model." A dataset of its traces is enough.
"If format reaches 100%, the student has learned to reason." Format shows it copied the layout, not that the reasoning works.
"Longer answers after distillation mean better reasoning." The student copies the teacher's length whether or not it helps.
"Testing on a few training problems is fine." Only held-out problems show whether the skill generalizes.
recallPrompts: What columns does camel-ai/gsm8k_distilled have, and which ones do we use?
Why do we drop traces longer than 1,024 tokens, and what side effect does that have?
What does completion_only_loss=True change during training?
Why do we use greedy decoding for the before/after comparison?
Why is the grader lenient (answer tag, then boxed, then last number)?
studyGuide.explainBackPrompt: Explain to a friend how you taught a small model to "think" by copying a bigger model's worked answers, and how you checked whether it really learned the skill or just the style. No code; use the exam-scripts picture or your own.

quiz.prompt: What does the camel-ai/gsm8k_distilled dataset provide for this lab?
options: GSM8K training problems with R1-style <think> reasoning traces and a boxed final answer
The weights of DeepSeek-R1
GSM8K test problems with their answers hidden
A reward model for maths
quiz.explanation: Each row has a problem, a reasoning_solution with a <think> block and a \boxed{} answer, the original GSM8K solution, and a success flag. We train on the traces and grade on the separate GSM8K test split.

quiz.prompt: What does completion_only_loss=True do in SFTConfig?
options: It stops training after one epoch
It removes the system prompt
It computes the loss only on the teacher's reply, not on the prompt
It makes the model generate shorter completions
quiz.explanation: With a prompt-completion dataset, the model is graded only on predicting the completion tokens. Learning to repeat the question back would waste capacity.

quiz.prompt: Why does the script set fp16=True and bf16=False on a free Colab T4?
options: fp16 gives more accurate results than bf16
The T4 GPU does not support bfloat16
LoRA only works in fp16
TRL requires fp16 for SFT
quiz.explanation: TRL turns on bf16 by default, but the T4 has no bfloat16 support, so the script checks torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() and falls back to float16 mixed precision.

quiz.prompt: Dropping traces longer than 1,024 tokens has which side effect?
options: The student learns from the teacher's shorter answers, nudging it toward a shorter style
The student can no longer use <think> tags
The test set gets smaller
Accuracy is guaranteed to drop
quiz.explanation: Distillation copies style as well as skill. Filtering to shorter traces means the student copies the teacher's more concise moments.

quiz.prompt: After training, format is near 100% and average tokens tripled, but accuracy barely moved. What's the best reading?
options: The run was a complete success
The evaluation must be broken
LoRA is not working
The student copied the teacher's style (layout and length) more than its skill
quiz.explanation: Format and length are easy to copy; accuracy shows whether the reasoning actually works. Read replies to see where the student's copied reasoning breaks down.

exercises.title: Add a strict grader next to the lenient one
hints: Use ANSWER_RE.findall and check the list has exactly one item.
Strip commas and $ before looking for numbers.
Return None whenever any rule fails, so None never equals the gold answer.

exercises.title: How many traces does a small student need?
hints: Change only N_TRAIN and num_train_epochs between runs.
Run the before evaluation once and reuse its numbers.
Restart the Colab runtime between runs to free GPU memory.
